title: Interleaved small+large request bursts causing batch fragmentation and KV-cache evictions — remediation plan
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2025-11-02 we observed repeated ~5–20s tail latency spikes for medium-length generation workloads during a sustained burst of mixed small (chat-like) and large (long completion) requests. The root cause analysis shows interleaving of small and large requests caused the continuous-batcher to prioritize small requests for slot allocation, which led to frequent KV-cache thrashing (evictions) on served model shards and highly fragmented batches. That fragmentation created repeated kernel warmups and cache misses, amplifying per-request latency and producing fairness skew for larger requests.

This ticket tracks remediation tasks, short-term mitigations and cross-team action items to prevent recurrence and improve observability of interleaved-burst failure modes.
investigation_findings: Batch formation logs show ~12% of batch windows contained >2 size classes during the incident window (vs 0.8% baseline)
KV-cache eviction rate rose by 7x correlated with arrival of medium-sized requests interleaved with many small requests
Scheduler metrics indicate priority inversion: small-request fast-path occupied hot slots causing large-request allocations to split across multiple GPUs
Tail latency correlated with cold-start kernel loads when a fragmented batch forced an alternate kernel path
Autoscaling and shard placement not directly responsible; root is scheduling/batching policy mismatch with mixed workload patterns
decisions: Implement temporary soft-throttling for smallest requests on overloaded serving nodes to stabilize batching until permanent scheduler changes land
Add size-class aware batching policy that prefers grouping similar sequence-length requests within a window (configurable threshold)
Expose per-slot KV-cache hit/miss and eviction counters in Console per-model dashboard for rapid triage
action_items: ENG-runtime: Add batch-size-class histogram to coalescer metrics (owner: Jordan Kim, estimate: 3d, due: 2025-11-12)
ENG-runtime: Implement a batching policy flag 'prefer_homogeneous_windows' with controlled rollout (owner: Priya Singh, estimate: 4, due: 2025-11-20)

ENG-infra: Deploy immediate soft-throttle rule for small requests on 3 worst-affected pools (owner: Marco Alvarez, estimate: 1, due: 2025-11-07) — temporary mitigation already applied at 2025-11-05 03:30 UTC
ENG-observability: Add KV-cache eviction heatmap to model dashboard and create an alert when eviction rate > 3x baseline for 5m (owner: Lea Zhou, estimate: 2, due: 2025-11-14)
ENG-schedulers: Prototype slot reservation heuristic that guarantees contiguous slots for large-request assemblies to avoid interleaving (owner: Luca Moreno, estimate: 5, due: 2025-12-01)
ENG-qe: Create a replay workload combining small/large interleaves and add to CI stability suite (owner: Sameer Rao, estimate: 3, due: 2025-11-18)
PM: Evaluate product-level rate limit defaults for chat vs completion APIs and document guidance (owner: Maya Chen, estimate: 2, due: 2025-11-21)
short_term_mitigations_completed: Soft-throttle rule applied to small-request class on affected pools (2025-11-05) — reduced eviction spike by ~60%
Temporary rollback of recent priority-adjustment config deployed to production (2025-11-05)
risks_and_tradeoffs: Soft-throttling small requests reduces immediate tail spikes but increases latency for some low-cost chat flows — acceptable as a temporary emergency mitigation
Homogeneous-window batching reduces fairness for mixed multiplexing use-cases if threshold is too aggressive; will require staged rollout and metrics guardrails
Slot reservation improves large-request latency but may decrease overall throughput under certain evenly-mixed workloads
follow_ups: Run 72-hour canary of 'prefer_homogeneous_windows' on runtime-1.22 canary fleet and compare token-per-second throughput and 99.9th latency (owner: Priya Singh)
Post-change user impact review with SRE/support for any latency regressions (owner: Asha Patel)
Update runbook playbook for continuous-batcher incidents with explicit steps for KV-eviction triage and temporary throttles (owner: Marco Alvarez)

2025-11-08 — Jordan Kim: Confirmed KV eviction metric now surfaces in ingestion pipeline; added test probe to replay harness.
2025-11-10 — Maya Chen (PM review): Approved product guidance draft. Please keep PM loop updated before releasing default flags.
